title: This Animal Finds Dinner by Knocking on Trees and Listening
subject: aye-aye

scenes.text: This animal finds its dinner by knocking on trees. Then it listens.
It taps on wood up to eight times every second with one very long, thin finger.
It is listening for an echo that sounds hollow, a hidden tunnel under the bark.
Then it gnaws a hole with its teeth, pushes in that bony middle finger, and hooks out the larvae.
Almost no other animal forages this way. Only the striped possum is known to do the same.
The aye-aye doesn't search for food. It knocks, and the tree answers.

description:
The aye-aye finds hidden insect larvae by tapping on wood and listening for hollow tunnels.
It taps up to eight times a second, then gnaws a hole and hooks the grub out with a long thin finger.
What other animal do you think should have a tool like this?
first_comment: If you could borrow one animal's trick for finding food, which would you choose?
